sentences.text: Culebrasuchus was a small animal, comparable in size to many living caimans.
This creature possessed upward-opening nostrils and non-overlapping skull bones around the supratemporal fenestrae, traits shared with other caimanines.
It had blunt rear teeth and an upper jaw that completely covered the lower jaw when closed, like modern caimanines.
Unlike its relatives, Culebrasuchus lacked ridges above its eye sockets and featured a notably large hole in its lower jaw.
The species had a straighter lower jaw than most alligatorids, lacked frontal bone ridges between eye sockets, and its largest upper jaw tooth was the fourth instead of the third.
The genus Culebrasuchus was named in 2013 by Hastings et al. based on a single skull and three neck vertebrae found in the Culebra Formation.
Studies confirm that Culebrasuchus is the most basal member of the subfamily Caimaninae within the family Alligatoridae.
Culebrasuchus lived between 18.5 and 16.3 million years ago during the Burdigalian stage.
It inhabited the Panama Canal Zone during the Early to Middle Miocene.
Researchers suggest the ancestors of Culebrasuchus likely lived in southern Mexico before the species moved into Panama.
Culebrasuchus was not the earliest caimanine, as other genera like Orthogenysuchus and Eocaiman lived in the Eocene, showing caimanines dispersed across oceans before the Isthmus of Panama formed.
